summary: Sweden’s mixed land-use and conservation framework assigns the country a 2030 LULUCF target of -3,955 Kt CO2eq under an EU-wide 310 Mt CO2-eq net-removals goal (reported as -310 Mt CO2-eq in sink accounting); the EU also seeks an additional 42 Mt CO2-eq relative to 2016–2018. Restoration passages cite measures across at least 20% of EU land areas and a 20% sea-area benchmark by 2030; no absolute Swedish restoration area is given. Sweden is already 68.5% forested, but no reforestation target is stated. Agriculture provisions are also EU-wide: 40% of CAP funding in 2023–2027 for climate objectives, at least 25% of annual direct-payment funds for eco-schemes, and 35% of Pillar II funds for environmental and climate activities. Sweden’s existing agricultural footprint is 38,942 km², or 8.7% of its land.
